s: A company's business owners require that 99.9% of checkout API requests each calendar month complete successfully in under 400 ms. The operations team wants to see how much of the monthly error budget remains and wants to be paged early if the budget is being used up too quickly. The services already send telemetry through CloudWatch Application Signals. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
o: Create a request-based service level objective (SLO) in CloudWatch Application Signals for the checkout operation with a 400 ms latency threshold, a 99.9% attainment goal and a monthly calendar interval. Create burn rate alarms on the SLO.
Create a CloudWatch alarm that fires when the Average latency of the checkout API exceeds 400 ms for 5 consecutive minutes.
Create AWS X-Ray groups for the checkout API and use X-Ray Insights notifications to detect latency anomalies.
Stream the application logs to Amazon OpenSearch Service and build a dashboard that calculates the share of requests under 400 ms each month.

w.y: This is 'translating business requirements to measurable metrics' (task 3.3). An Application Signals SLO turns the requirement directly into an SLI (latency of the checkout operation), a goal (99.9% of requests) and an interval (calendar month). It tracks attainment and the remaining error budget, and burn rate alarms warn when the budget is being consumed faster than the goal allows.

o.A: Correct. Built-in SLO, error budget and burn rate alarms; nothing to build.
o.B: An average hides the slow tail and does not measure '99.9% of requests', and a 5-minute alarm has no notion of a monthly budget.
o.C: Insights flags anomalies but does not track an SLO or error budget against a business target.
o.D: It can be built, but it is custom work to create and maintain, which is more overhead than a managed SLO.

s: Service level objectives (SLOs) in Application Signals
